newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden bourse says noted heavy Trelleborg trade.
newsitem.headline: Sweden bourse says noted heavy Trelleborg trade.

text.p: Stockholm's Stock Exchange said on Tuesday it was aware of heavy dealing in mining group Trelleborg AB by brokers Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) ahead of last week's billion dollar financing deal co-arranged by DMG.

Stock Exchange spokesman Mats Wilhelmsson declined to say if the exchange was investigating the DMG dealing. "Of course it raises questions in my mind, but I can't say more than that. That's why we're here," he told Reuters.
Mats Andersson, head of DMG's Swedish equity operation, said there was no connection between its dominance of market trade in Trelleborg and of Trelleborg's finance deal.
"We've had an overweight recommendation on the share for the past six months," Andersson said. "I've no idea at all what they do on the loan side. Our 'Chinese walls' are completely watertight.

"They (the volume figures) are high, yes, but on the other hand I would argue that since we are focusing on institutional investors that means that we get the kind of orders that we have had in Trelleborg," he said.
"And you have the same pattern in very many other shares where we from time to time are among the big ones," he added.
Wilhelmsson, head of the Stock Exchange market surveillance unit, said, "Of course dealing like this isn't usual, but it is common that brokers' firms deal a lot in the firms they are involved in."

Shortly before the Stockholm bourse opened on Thursday, Trelleborg announced a $1.0 billion long-term refinancing deal which took the form of a 22-bank syndicated loan co-arranged by DMG, Enskilda and Handelsbanken Markets.

DMG has dominated net buying (total purchases minus total sales) of Trelleborg stock in recent weeks, acquiring a total of 1.57 million B-series shares over the ten trading days to October 2, the day before the loan was announced.
This corresponded to 84 percent of all brokers' net buying of Trelleborg's B-series share over the period.

On October 2, the trading day immediately prior to the announcement of the syndicated loan, DMG brokers net bought 463,000 Trelleborg shares to a value of 41.7 million crowns, and accounted for 86 percent of all net buying.
Total turnover in Trelleborg B shares on October 2 was 1,158,000 shares, compared with an average turnover of 354,000 for the nine preceding trading days.
Turnover has since fallen back to an average of 446,000 over the three bourse days following the announcement.
DMG accounted for 22 percent of turnover -- buying and selling -- in Trelleborg's B-series share in the ten trading days up to and including October 2.
During that time, its share of total trades of all instruments on the Stockholm bourse was just 2.7 percent.

DMG's Andersson said DMG had advised its clients to increase exposure to Trelleborg. On September 17, DMG repeated an "overweight" recommendation on Trelleborg, saying the company was seriously undervalued.
Swedish legislation forbids stockbrokers from share trading using price-sensitive information that is not freely available to the public.
Investment banks with stockbroking operations are obliged to set up "Chinese walls" to prevent the spread of information between stockbroking and other investment banking operations.

Trelleborg's share price was not moved markedly by the news of the finance deal. The share rose two crowns to 91 during morning trade on October 3, but fell back one to close at 90 crowns. It has since hovered around the 91 crown level.
Trelleborg said the loan would mean cheaper financing with a longer duration, and that it would give the company greater scope for expansive investments.
Industry analysts said the loan could be a precursor to a major acquisition, but Trelleborg spokesman Leif Oberg declined to provide further details.

"We have no comments today on what we should do with the revolving credit facility. It's wait and see. We have a strategic plan that means expansion, organically and by acquisition, in the areas where we work today," he told Reuters.
-- Trevor Datson, Stockholm newsroom, +46-8-700 1006
